Module 0 of the course. Read this first.

[Moving] = a version, date, list or status that was still changing when written (it has an "as of" date). [Old wording] = a name or number that older material and questions still use. Independence, Trademarks and Good Study Habits

html:
1What You Will Learn

  • State the exam format, the pass mark and the validity
  • Name the four domains and their weights
  • Read the course labels, and meet the Harbor Books case
  • Know that the course is independent and educational

2The KCNA Exam in NumbersMoving

  • 60 multiple-choice questions in 90 minutes
  • The pass mark is 75%: that is 45 of 60 correct
  • It is taken online with a proctor, and results come by email within 24 hours
  • That is about 90 seconds a question; Module 16 shows how to use the time
  • As of 30 October 2026: these are the figures on the Linux Foundation pages; confirm them on the LF site before you book

Exam tip: Plan for about 90 seconds a question, and flag the hard ones for later.

3Booking, Validity and RenewalMoving

Topic What to know
Prerequisites none
Booking window 12 months to schedule and take the exam
Validity the result stays valid for 2 years
Renewal passing the CKA or the CKAD (the administrator and application developer exams) renews the KCNA
Price and retakes not stated in this course: the pages change and do not agree, so check the LF site
  • As of 30 October 2026: this is what the Linux Foundation pages say

Exam tip: Book when you are ready, not when the window is about to close.

4The Curriculum: Four DomainsMoving

  • Kubernetes Fundamentals, 44%: Module 1 to Module 5
  • Container Orchestration, 28%: Module 6 to Module 9
  • Cloud Native Application Delivery, 16%: Module 10 and Module 11
  • Cloud Native Architecture, 12%: Module 12 to Module 14
  • 13 topics in all; the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) publishes domain weights, not weights per topic
  • As of 30 October 2026: this curriculum applies to exams taken from late November 2025 onward

Exam tip: The biggest domain is Kubernetes Fundamentals: give it the most study time.

5Old Curriculum, New CurriculumOld wording

Old domain (weight) Where it is now
Kubernetes Fundamentals (46%) Kubernetes Fundamentals (44%)
Container Orchestration (22%) Container Orchestration (28%)
Cloud Native Architecture (16%) Cloud Native Architecture (12%)
Cloud Native Observability (8%) inside Cloud Native Architecture: Module 13
Cloud Native Application Delivery (8%) Cloud Native Application Delivery (16%)
  • Older prep material uses the five-domain split, so you may meet its names
  • Old sub-topics such as Prometheus, Cost Management and Service Mesh still appear in this course, under their new homes

Exam tip: If a question uses an old name, map it to its new home and answer the same way.

6Where the KCNA SitsMoving

  • The KCNA and the KCSA (the cloud native security associate exam) are multiple-choice associate exams
  • The CKA (administrator), CKAD (application developer) and CKS (security specialist) are performance-based: you solve tasks in a command line
  • The CKS requires that you pass the CKA first
  • Newer exams such as the CNPA exist too; this is a map, not a sales pitch
  • As of 30 October 2026: this is the family listed on the Linux Foundation pages

Exam tip: The KCNA tests knowledge; the hands-on exams test doing.

7How the Course Is Organized

  • 17 modules, numbered 00 to 16: 14 content modules in the four domains, plus this introduction, a quick-reference recap and exam technique
  • Each content module has objectives, a case check-in, teaching slides, a recap, practice questions and answers at a glance
  • There are 105 practice questions, each with four options and one correct answer
  • The script asks the question, pauses, then gives the answer and the reason
  • Every teaching slide ends with an Exam Tip

Exam tip: Answer each question before the pause ends, then read the reason.

8Labels You Will See

Label What it tells you
Beyond the curriculum useful context that the curriculum does not list; lower priority for the exam
Archived topic from the earlier curriculum, or at recognition level: know what it is and what it is for
Moving a fact that changes over time; the slide gives an "as of" date
Old wording a name that older material still uses
  • Slides without a label cover the current curriculum directly

Exam tip: Spend your first study hours on slides with no label, and your last on the labeled ones.

9Meet Harbor Books, the Running Case

  • The shop: Harbor Books, a fictional online bookshop; nothing in it comes from a real company or a real exam
  • The parts: storefront, catalog, orders, postgres, cache, mailer and nightly-report
  • The clusters: one for production and one for staging, with the namespaces shop and platform
  • The people: a developer, a platform engineer, a security lead and a shop owner
  • The story: a monolith grows into services, and the team adopts Kubernetes to run them safely

Exam tip: The case only gives you a story to hang each idea on; the exam asks about the idea.

10Independence, Trademarks and Good Study Habits

  • This course is independent: it is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Linux Foundation or the CNCF
  • It is educational, not official exam preparation; KCNA, Kubernetes, CNCF and the project names belong to their owners
  • The course shows no logos, and gives no price or retake terms
  • Confirm exam facts on the Linux Foundation site before you book
  • Study well: answer before the pause, read the reason, and repeat the questions you missed

Exam tip: A study plan beats a long cram: a little every day, with questions.

11Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
The exam 60 multiple-choice questions, 90 minutes, 75% to pass, online and proctored
Booking 12 months to schedule, valid for 2 years, renewed by the CKA or the CKAD
The curriculum four domains, with Kubernetes Fundamentals the largest; older material uses five
The course 14 content modules, labels for Beyond the curriculum, Archived topic, Moving and Old wording
The notice independent, educational, no logos; confirm the facts on the LF site
